title: How flamingos in Albania sparked massive protests
description:
What began as a peaceful protest in Albania turned violent in October, as students took the lead, setting buildings on fire and clashing with police. They are demanding better university conditions, greater opportunities for young people – and an end to what they describe as a corrupt government.

This all goes back to a proposal to build a huge, luxury tourist resort in Zvërnec, where there’s a flamingo reserve. US President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner, is among the investors. But locals were unhappy at the impact the proposals would have on the flamingos and the nature in the area. So, they began to protest.

The Flamingo Movement has grown, and crowds are now chanting not just about the environment, but schools, jobs and living standards. We hear from some protesters, including 23-year-old activist, Brunela, who has become known as “the girl who started the revolution”. And Rita Behadini from the What in the World, breaks down the political landscape of Albania.

summaryEn: This episode of What in the World explores how an environmental campaign to protect a flamingo reserve in Zvërnec, Albania, developed into a student-led national movement known as the Flamingo Revolution. The protests initially targeted plans for a luxury resort backed by investors including Jared Kushner. However, widespread frustration over government corruption, high unemployment, poor public services, and severe youth brain drain drove thousands of students to the streets of Tirana. Led by activists like 23-year-old Brunela Mertiri, demonstrators are calling for systemic reform and the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama, who refuses to step down despite violent clashes between police and protesters.
